newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa market lacks consumer interest.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa market lacks consumer interest.

text.p: German cocoa traders said processors were showing no interest in the market for beans or butter as some factories were planning reduced schedules next week to follow on from the Easter holiday weekend.
Spot and afloat beans were offered at low differentials but consumers showed no reaction.
"The industry still needs a lot of cover throughout 1997, but my clients are happy to stay away for now," one trader said.
"They were last in the market when sterling hit six-week lows on March 18," he added.
Traders said prospects of a comfortable West African crop scenario -- with Ivory Coast arrivals pointing to a crop perhaps in excess of 1.1 million tonnes -- encouraged the passive attitude.
Second quarter cif Ivorian bean sellers were little changed on the previous fortnight at 2.67 marks/kg, with spot prices ex-local stocks at 2.70 marks.
Cocoa butter prices liquid ex-works were 6.92 marks/kg on average for the second quarter (ratio at 2.54) versus 6.95 marks/kg asked a fortnight ago on the basis of a ratio at 2.58.
Spot butter ex-stocks cost 6.92 marks, with the ratio at 2.52.
Fourth quarter 1997 cocoa butter offers were made on a basis of a ratio of 2.55, with buyers at 2.53.
Sterling was at 2.7190 marks at the Frankfurt Exchange Fixing at midday.
